messages:
sophia: FYI I ran the 50B q4f16 bring-up across eu-west and us-west to sanity-check latency/concurrency for Dedicated. Need a quick gut check on how many GPUs to provision per slab and what autoscale headroom looks like.
max: Awesome — can you paste the p50/p95/p99 numbers and concurrency target?
lee: pasted raw run below (small samples, cold start trimmed):
```
model: 50b-q4f16
region eu-west (h100): concurrency 8 -> p50 62ms, p95 190ms, p99 420ms, qps @8=450
region us-west (a100): concurrency 8 -> p50 84ms, p95 240ms, p99 560ms, qps @8=380
seq_len=1024, batcher continuous, kernel=attn-tiling-v2 for H100 / attn-tiling-v1 fallback on A100
mem footprints: H100 ~ 40GB used, A100 ~ 48GB used
```
sophia: thanks. those p99s are higher than expected in us-west — note a100 runs the older tile kernel which increases tail. H100 warm slab had KV cache warmups that helped.
chris: for Dedicated capacity sizing we target p99 SLO headroom = 1.5x observed p99 under steady traffic + burst runway for 20% microbursts. So eu-west per-slab capacity at concurrency 8 -> plan 2x slab headroom = two GPUs per slab? math: if qps@8=450, one slab = 450 qps, target runway 675 qps per slab -> we want ~1.5x machines = safe to put 1 slab per GPU but keep autoscale to add a 2nd slab on spikes.
jordan: ops-bot logs show warmup behavior: first 5 minutes after deploy p99 spikes x2 then levels. We should reserve warmup buffer for canaries only.
max: what's the recommended GPU count per Dedicated pool for initial rollout (1000 qps steady in eu-west, 600 qps steady in us-west)?
lee: quick calc: eu-west: 1000 / 450 ~= 2.2 slabs -> with 1 slab per GPU that's 3 GPUs baseline. Add 20% autoscale headroom -> 4 GPUs. us-west: 600 / 380 ~= 1.6 -> 2 GPUs baseline, +1 headroom -> 3 GPUs.
sophia: also consider kernel fallback: if H100 nodes fail and traffic routes to A100, p99 jumps ~30-40%. So cross-region fallback would require extra capacity. Suggest cross-region fallback margin = +30% to baseline.
chris: agreed. So final proposal: eu-west Dedicated: baseline 3 GPUs, autoscale ceiling 5; us-west Dedicated: baseline 2 GPUs, autoscale ceiling 4. Include a canary slab with half traffic to detect regressions for 10m rollouts.
max: can we express this as simple runbook bullets for infra provisioning? I can hand to procurement.
sophia: runbook bullets: 1) Create Dedicated pool eu-west: 3 H100 GPUs baseline, autoscale max 5, concurrency target per GPU=8, canary slab (1 GPU) with 5-10% traffic. 2) Create Dedicated pool us-west: 2 A100 GPUs baseline, autoscale max 4, concurrency target per GPU=8, canary slab. 3) Configure routing policy: prefer local region H100, fallback to A100 with +30% capacity margin. 4) Monitor p99 and droplet warmup; rollback threshold p99>700ms or error rate>1.5%.
jordan: ops-bot: added a provisioning ticket #DL-1729 with requested counts and tags.
ops-bot: ticket DL-1729 created: eu-west 3->5 H100 pool, us-west 2->4 A100 pool, canary tagging set. ETA vendor quote in 2 business days.
lee: one more thought — if we enable q8a quant profile for A100 we shave ~10-15% latency at cost of slight quality delta. Would be good to run a quick eval before finalizing.
sophia: good call, schedule short eval: q4f16 (baseline) vs q8a on A100, 10k prompts, measure ROUGE/utility and p99. If quality drop <1% then allow q8a on fallback path.
chris: I'll add the eval to the playbook and set alerting for quality regression tied to canary.
max: perfect. I'll convert sophia's runbook bullets into the final capacity request and sync with finance. :thumbsup:
sophia: thanks everyone — follow-ups: lee to run q8a eval, chris to add playbook alerts, ops to track ticket. I'll post a short summary after results. :white_check_mark:
